source (URL or citation): TechCrunch, 2025-06-06; Washington Times, 2025-06-19; The Niche (ipscell.com), 2025-11; MIT Technology Review, 2025-12-05

one-line 2026-side claim: Selecting the top-scoring of ten IVF embryos on a cognitive polygenic score yields an expected gain of about 2.5 IQ points GIVEN THEN-CURRENT PREDICTORS — the paper states expected gain scales with the square root of the variance the score explains, so this is not a fixed ceiling — with wide prediction intervals; in real families of up to 20 offspring the top-scoring sibling for height was the tallest in only about 25% of families
source (URL or citation): Karavani et al., "Screening Human Embryos for Polygenic Traits Has Limited Utility", Cell 179(6), 1424-1435 (Nov 2019)

one-line 2026-side claim: He Jiankui announced CCR5-edited twin girls in November 2018; a third gene-edited child was born to a different mother in 2019, acknowledged by the court that in December 2019 convicted him of illegal medical practice, sentenced him to three years, fined him and banned him for life from reproductive medicine. No further gene-edited births have been reported since, and heritable editing is prohibited by policy in the large majority of countries with any policy
source (URL or citation): MIT Technology Review and STAT, 2019-12-30; Center for Genetics and Society; Journal of Law and the Biosciences 6(1), 2019

one-line 2026-side claim: Life-expectancy improvements decelerated after 1990 across the eight longest-lived populations plus Hong Kong and the US; without breakthroughs that slow aging itself, radical life extension is judged implausible this century, and no national average approaches 100
source (URL or citation): Olshansky et al., "Implausibility of radical life extension in humans in the twenty-first century", Nature Aging (2024-10-07), doi:10.1038/s43587-024-00702-3

one-line 2026-side claim: Programmable implanted drug pumps (intrathecal delivery) and subdermal hormone implants are routine clinical devices; note that routine insulin pumps are external continuous-subcutaneous systems, fully implanted insulin pumps being rare and specialised; no space agency has proposed or performed removal of the digestive tract for spaceflight, and crew health programmes rely on pharmacology, exercise and shielding
source (URL or citation): Medtronic SynchroMed intrathecal drug delivery; etonogestrel subdermal implants (Nexplanon); NASA Human Research Program countermeasure literature

one-line 2026-side claim: Dor Yeshorim, founded 1983 by Rabbi Josef Ekstein, screens young people in Orthodox Jewish communities for recessive-disease carrier status and issues an anonymous ID number; when a match is proposed the two numbers are checked together, typically before the couple meets, and the answer returned is that the pair may proceed or is incompatible. Disease only — no traits are screened. It tests roughly 25,000 people a year across about 11 countries and has screened several hundred thousand since 1983
source (URL or citation): Dor Yeshorim process and FAQ pages (doryeshorim.org); Ekstein & Katzenstein, "The Dor Yeshorim Story: Community-Based Carrier Screening for Tay-Sachs Disease", Advances in Genetics 44 (2001); Hadassah Magazine, 2017

one-line 2026-side claim: Mid-1960s baseline for ch. 2: de Latil's Thinking by Machine (1956), whose classification of effectors Lem builds on; Lévi-Strauss (1952) on the statistics of technogenesis; the Apollo programme under way at roughly $20bn; cross-Channel hovercraft entering service; the Harrier's precursor (Hawker P.1127) flying since 1960
source (URL or citation): Pierre de Latil, La Pensee Artificielle (1953) / Thinking by Machine (1956); Levi-Strauss, Race and History (1952); NASA Apollo programme cost records; Hawker P.1127 first hover 1960; Hoverlloyd/Hoverspeed SR.N4 cross-Channel car ferry service from 1968. one-line 2026-side claim: Electric cars (battery and plug-in hybrid) reached 25% of global new car sales in 2025, so at least three-quarters of new cars still have a combustion engine (over 20 million sold, up 20% on 2024): about 55% of sales in China, 28% in Europe, just under 10% in the United States
source (URL or citation): IEA, Global EV Outlook 2026, "Trends in electric cars"; IEA news, 2025

one-line 2026-side claim: California requires most newly manufactured small off-road engines — spark-ignition petrol engines at or below 25 hp, covering lawnmowers and leaf blowers — to be zero-emission from 1 January 2024; existing equipment may still be used and sold second-hand
source (URL or citation): California Air Resources Board, "CARB approves updated regulations requiring most new small off-road engines be zero emission by 2024" (Dec 2021); CARB SORE regulation, phase one effective 2024-01-01

one-line 2026-side claim: The car-carrying cross-Channel hovercraft service ended on 1 October 2000, the SR.N4s beaten by the Channel Tunnel and the end of duty-free; large commercial hovercraft effectively disappeared, with the Southsea–Ryde route remaining one of very few scheduled hovercraft services in the world
source (URL or citation): BBC News, "Hovercraft crew mark 10 years since final Dover flight" (2010); Hoverspeed / SR.N4 service records; Hovertravel Southsea–Ryde

one-line 2026-side claim: Fixed-wing aircraft did acquire vertical take-off by vectoring thrust and stayed in production: the Harrier family entered service in 1969, the F-35B (short take-off / vertical landing) reached initial operating capability in 2015, and the V-22 tiltrotor entered service in 2007 — all military, none replacing the helicopter
source (URL or citation): Programme records: Hawker Siddeley Harrier (1969); Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey (USMC IOC 2007); Lockheed Martin F-35B (USMC IOC July 2015)

one-line 2026-side claim: No US electric vertical-take-off aircraft holds an FAA type certificate as of mid-2026: Joby has reached stage four of the FAA's five-stage type-certification process and Archer has closed phase three, both targeting certification by late 2026 or 2027, with an FAA pilot programme allowing pre-certification demonstration flights
source (URL or citation): FAA certification trackers and company disclosures, 2026; Joby Aviation stage-4 / Type Inspection Authorization reporting, March 2026

one-line 2026-side claim: From about 2023 several manufacturers (including BMW, Mazda, Volkswagen, Tesla and Ford) dropped AM radio from electric or hybrid models, citing interference from high-voltage components; Congress responded with the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, which would mandate AM reception from model year 2028: S. 315 was reintroduced 2025-01-29 and advanced by the Senate Commerce Committee on 2025-02-05, and as of the cosponsor lists checked on 2026-08-18 it had exactly 60 Senate cosponsors (plus the sponsor), while the House companion H.R. 979 had 317
source (URL or citation): congress.gov cosponsor lists for S. 315 and H.R. 979 (119th Congress), read 2026-08-18 (60 and 317 respectively; latest House cosponsor dated 2025-11-07); Senate Commerce Committee advance 2025-02-05; contemporaneous reporting 2023-2025. NB secondary sources saying 'more than 60 Senators' count the sponsor

one-line 2026-side claim: COBOL written for mid-20th-century mainframes is still in production at scale — estimates run from roughly 220 billion to 800 billion lines in active use — underpinning a large share of core banking, with widely cited figures of about 95% of US ATM transactions and trillions of dollars of daily processing
source (URL or citation): Micro Focus COBOL survey (2022); IBM, "What is COBOL modernization?"; Planet Mainframe (2024) and industry estimates. NB the line-count and percentage figures are industry estimates, not audited

one-line 2026-side claim: The result that started the deep-learning era was trained on graphics processors built for rendering: Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton trained AlexNet on two consumer GTX 580 GPUs, a cross-over between video-game hardware and statistical learning
source (URL or citation): Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, "ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks", NIPS 2012

one-line 2026-side claim: Mid-1960s baseline for ch. 3: Shklovsky's Universe, Life, Intelligence (1962); the Cocconi-Morrison proposal (1959) and Drake's Project Ozma at Green Bank from 1960; the 1964 Byurakan conference where Kardashev proposed his three-type scale; no exoplanet had been detected, and estimates assumed roughly 1 star in 150 had planets
source (URL or citation): I. S. Shklovsky, Universe, Life, Intelligence (1962); Cocconi & Morrison, Nature 184 (1959); Project Ozma (1960); Byurakan conference (1964); Kardashev (1964)

one-line 2026-side claim: NASA's High Resolution Microwave Survey, the last major US federally funded SETI programme, began observing in October 1992 and was killed roughly a year later by a Senate amendment from Richard Bryan (D-NV); it cost about $10 million a year, under 0.1% of NASA's budget
source (URL or citation): High Resolution Microwave Survey programme records; contemporaneous reporting on the 1993 appropriations amendment; Scientific American, "NASA Should Start Funding SETI Again"

one-line 2026-side claim: Breakthrough Listen, announced by Yuri Milner with Stephen Hawking at the Royal Society on 20 July 2015, committed $100 million of private money over ten years — roughly $10 million a year — to the largest search for extraterrestrial intelligence yet mounted
source (URL or citation): Breakthrough Initiatives announcement, 2015-07-20; Breakthrough Listen programme documentation

one-line 2026-side claim: The Allen Telescope Array, built with about $30 million from Paul Allen, went into hibernation in April 2011 after NSF radio-observatory funding fell to roughly a tenth of its former level and California state support was cut; it resumed operations in December 2011 partly by taking US Air Force money to track orbital debris, plus about $200,000 raised from the public
source (URL or citation): Forbes and BBC reporting, April 2011; Universe Today, "Budget Woes Put SETI's Allen Telescope Array into Hibernation"; SETI Institute SETIStars campaign records

one-line 2026-side claim: The SETI Institute announced on 8 November 2023 a $200 million bequest from the estate of Qualcomm co-founder Franklin Antonio, who died in May 2022 — its largest gift ever, against an annual operating budget of roughly $25-30 million
source (URL or citation): SETI Institute announcement, 2023-11-08; Philanthropy News Digest; The Register, 2023-11-09

one-line 2026-side claim: Deliberate transmission remains rare and contested: a 2015 statement issued around the AAAS meeting held that the decision whether to transmit "must be based upon a worldwide consensus, and not a decision based upon the wishes of a few individuals with access to powerful communications equipment"; the main transmissions to date were a handful sent by Alexander Zaitsev from the Evpatoria dish, and METI International was founded in 2015 to send more
source (URL or citation): 2015 statement on messaging extraterrestrial intelligence (setiathome.berkeley.edu/meti_statement_0.html); Zaitsev's Evpatoria transmissions; METI International founding, July 2015

one-line 2026-side claim: Radio SETI searches concentrate on narrowband signals precisely because natural astrophysical emission is broadband while an efficiently encoded transmission is statistically indistinguishable from noise; beacons are therefore expected to be simple and repetitive rather than information-dense
source (URL or citation): Standard SETI search methodology; "The Search for Technosignatures: a Review of Possibilities" (arXiv:2605.21093) and the narrowband-drift search literature

one-line 2026-side claim: Public spending on nuclear-energy research runs orders of magnitude above the search: the US Fusion Energy Sciences programme alone was $790 million in FY2025, and ITER's construction cost has grown past $20 billion, with US contributions exceeding $2.9 billion from 2007 to 2023
source (URL or citation): DOE FY2025 Budget in Brief; Congressional Research Service R48362, "ITER - An International Nuclear Fusion Research and Development Facility" (2025)

one-line 2026-side claim: Breakthrough Starshot, announced in April 2016 with $100 million of private funding, proposes gram-scale laser-driven sails rather than a crewed ship — the only funded interstellar flight programme, and privately funded like the listening
source (URL or citation): Breakthrough Initiatives, Starshot announcement, April 2016

one-line 2026-side claim: Mid-1960s baseline for ch. 1: Blackett's Military and Political Consequences of Atomic Energy (1948), which Lem grades; Thirring's Die Geschichte der Atombombe (1946); Bellamy's Looking Backward (1888), set in 2000; the "balance of fear" then about fifteen years old; and controlled fusion widely expected within decades
source (URL or citation): P. M. S. Blackett, Military and Political Consequences of Atomic Energy (1948); Hans Thirring (1946); Edward Bellamy, Looking Backward: 2000-1887 (1888)

one-line 2026-side claim: Summa Technologiae was first published in Polish in 1964 and reissued that year, with altered editions in 1967 and 1974; Zylinska's English translation (Minnesota, 2013) follows the fourth edition of 1974, which Lem corrected and updated partly on reader feedback. Lem's essays "Twenty Years Later" (1982, appended to the fourth Polish edition) and "Thirty Years Later" are not included in this English edition
source (URL or citation): Joanna Zylinska, translator's introduction to Summa Technologiae (University of Minnesota Press, 2013), pp. 20-21, citing Butko; table of contents of the 2013 edition (Translator's Introduction, chs. 1-8, Conclusion, Notes, Bibliography, Index)

one-line 2026-side claim: Wright, Kanodia & Lubar built an eight-dimensional model of the radio-SETI search space and computed how much of it has been examined: the fraction searched is minute, comparable to having examined a drinking glass of seawater for fish in all Earth's oceans; a later survey using the same framework reported a search fraction of about 2e-16
source (URL or citation): Wright, Kanodia & Lubar, "How Much SETI Has Been Done? Finding Needles in the n-dimensional Cosmic Haystack", Astronomical Journal 156, 260 (2018), arXiv:1809.07252; Tremblay & Tingay, MWA Vela survey (PASA, 2020)

one-line 2026-side claim: Deliberate interstellar transmission did happen once with fanfare: Frank Drake's Arecibo message was broadcast toward the globular cluster M13 in 1974
source (URL or citation): SETI Institute, history of the Arecibo message (1974)

one-line 2026-side claim: Breakthrough Listen's observing is done on publicly owned instruments rather than its own: principally the NSF-funded Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope and CSIRO's Parkes (Murriyang) dish, from which it has aggregated more than 20 petabytes of radio data
source (URL or citation): Breakthrough Listen telescope partnerships and programme description; Isaacson et al., "The Breakthrough Listen Search for Intelligent Life" (arXiv:1907.05519)

one-line 2026-side claim: Tetlock followed 284 experts' political and economic forecasts from 1984 for two decades and found their accuracy barely distinguishable from chance — the "dart-throwing chimpanzee" result — published as Expert Political Judgment (2005)
source (URL or citation): Philip E. Tetlock, Expert Political Judgment: How Good Is It? How Can We Know? (Princeton, 2005)

one-line 2026-side claim: In IARPA's forecasting tournament (2011-2015) the Good Judgment Project's "superforecasters" were about 30% more accurate than US intelligence analysts with access to classified material, and beat rival teams by margins of roughly 35-72%
source (URL or citation): Tetlock & Gardner, Superforecasting (2015); IARPA ACE tournament results; Good Judgment Project records

one-line 2026-side claim: A survey of 2,778 researchers published in top AI venues put a 50% chance of high-level machine intelligence by 2047 — thirteen years earlier than the same series' estimate from a survey conducted one year before
source (URL or citation): Grace et al., "Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI" (2024), AI Impacts; earlier waves 2016 (2061) and 2022 (2050)

one-line 2026-side claim: No spent nuclear fuel has yet been permanently disposed of: Finland's Onkalo, the world's first deep geological repository, was still awaiting its government operating licence as of August 2026, with disposal yet to begin
source (URL or citation): Posiva press release on STUK's safety assessment, 2026; Finnish regulator (STUK) licensing status

one-line 2026-side claim: The selection effect Lem describes in note 10 to ch. 8 — repeated testing leaving a residue of investigators with apparently significant results — was named and formalised fifteen years later as the file-drawer problem
source (URL or citation): Robert Rosenthal, "The 'File Drawer Problem' and Tolerance for Null Results", Psychological Bulletin 86(3), 638-641 (1979)

one-line 2026-side claim: Lem assessed Summa's predictive accuracy in three later essay collections — The Mystery of the Chinese Room (1996), The Megabit Bomb (1999) and The Blink of an Eye (2000) — claiming among his successes the adaptive morphology of the human brain, biocomputing, and autonomous search engines, which he called ariadnology. None of these collections is held here; the account is Swirski's
source (URL or citation): Swirski, "The Cassandra Syndrome" (2022), reporting Lem's self-assessments; Swirski, A Stanislaw Lem Reader (Northwestern, 1997)

one-line 2026-side claim: Peter Butko, a biophysicist, assessed Summa chapter by chapter in 2006, before any English translation existed, and described the book as "essentially a work in progress" that Lem corrected and updated on reader feedback — the judgement Zylinska quotes in her introduction
source (URL or citation): Peter Butko, "Summa technologiae – Looking Back and Ahead", in Swirski (ed.), The Art and Science of Stanislaw Lem (McGill-Queen's, 2006), pp. 81-103
